result.overall: The court allowed the judicial review, finding the Refugee Appeal Division's decision unreasonable due to flawed implausibility findings and improper corroboration requirements.

themes.name: Implausibility Findings
themes.summary: The RAD found parts of the claimant's story implausible without sufficient basis, relying on speculation rather than evidence.

themes.name: Requirement for Corroboration
themes.summary: The RAD required corroboration without properly explaining why it was necessary or whether such evidence was reasonably available.

themes.name: Assessment of Corroborating Evidence
themes.summary: The RAD rejected some corroborating evidence reasonably but failed to address a key letter from a friend, contributing to unreasonableness.

themes.name: Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) Analysis
themes.summary: The RAD confused the IFA analysis with the well-founded fear of persecution, failing to properly assess if relocation would protect the claimant.

arguments.claim: The RAD erred in finding his story implausible without a firm basis.
arguments.quote: the RAD did not explain the basis for its implausibility findings

arguments.claim: The RAD wrongly required corroboration without explaining why it was necessary or why evidence was reasonably available.
arguments.quote: the RAD appears to have started from the premise that there is a general requirement for corroboration

arguments.claim: The RAD rejected corroborating evidence without adequate reasons and failed to address a letter from a friend.
arguments.quote: The RAD should have responded to this argument

arguments.claim: The RAD's IFA finding independently justifies dismissal of the claim.
arguments.quote: the RAD confused the two issues, at least in significant part

holdings.statement: The standard of review on judicial review in immigration and refugee matters is reasonableness.
holdings.quote: On an application for judicial review in immigration and refugee matters, the standard of review is reasonableness

holdings.statement: Implausibility findings may be made only in the clearest of cases where facts are outside what could reasonably be expected or contradicted by documentary evidence.
holdings.quote: plausibility findings should be made only in the clearest of cases

holdings.statement: A decision-maker can require corroboration only if there is an independent reason such as doubts about credibility, implausibility, or reliance on hearsay, and the evidence is reasonably available.
holdings.quote: a decision-maker can only require corroborative evidence if: The decision-maker clearly sets out an independent reason for requiring corroboration

holdings.statement: The RAD's implausibility findings and requirement for corroboration lacked a rational chain of analysis and were unreasonable.
holdings.quote: the RAD’s decision does not exhibit a rational chain of analysis

holdings.statement: The RAD's IFA analysis was flawed by conflating it with the well-founded fear of persecution analysis and cannot sustain the decision alone.
holdings.quote: the RAD confused the two issues, at least in significant part

holdings.statement: The matter is sent back to the RAD for redetermination due to the unreasonableness of its decision.
holdings.quote: the application for judicial review will be allowed and the matter will be sent back for redetermination

rebuttals.point: The RAD's IFA finding independently justifies dismissal of the claim.
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD confused the IFA analysis with the well-founded fear of persecution and failed to properly assess the protective effect of relocation.
rebuttals.quote: the RAD confused the two issues, at least in significant part

authorities.authority: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.why: Established the reasonableness standard of review and requirement for a rational chain of analysis.
authorities.quote: the standard of review is reasonableness

authorities.authority: Valtchev v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2001 FCT 776
authorities.why: Implausibility findings require the clearest of cases.
authorities.quote: plausibility findings should be made only in the clearest of cases

authorities.authority: Horvath v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2018 CF 147
authorities.why: Corroboration required only if there is reason to doubt credibility and evidence is reasonably available.
authorities.quote: Corroborative evidence was only required if the RAD had (1) reason to doubt the Applicants’ claim and (2) the corroborating evidence could reasonably be expected to be available

authorities.authority: Maldonado v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1980] 2 FC 302 (CA)
authorities.why: Presumption of truthfulness unless reason to doubt.
authorities.quote: When an applicant swears to the truth of certain allegations, this creates a presumption that those allegations are true unless there be reason to doubt their truthfulness

authorities.authority: Chaudhry v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2020 FC 902
authorities.why: Discussed the need to separate IFA analysis from well-founded fear of persecution.
authorities.quote: care must be taken to separate the IFA analysis from that of the well-founded fear of persecution
